## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Session
where: BookingRepository (uses), src/persistence/bookingRepository.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
findBySession(sessionId: string): Booking[] {
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Skating Session

=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const session = this.sessions.findById(input.sessionId);
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: A and B are the same concept: the ice-rink session that bookings are made against. A's BookingRepository.findBySession(sessionId) looks up bookings by a session id. B's BookingService looks up that same session with this.sessions.findById(input.sessionId), which the graph shows as SessionRepository.findById. Other services in the graph (IceMonitorService, HireStockRepository, SessionService.availability) point to a skating-rink domain, so "Session" and "Skating Session" are two names for one thing. This is more than a shared id: both pieces of code refer to the same session that holds bookings.
